verses.restored: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession.

familiar.text: But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession,

modern.text: Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property.

original.text: Ἀνὴρ δέ τις Ἁνανίας ὀνόματι σὺν Σαπφίρῃ τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπώλησεν κτῆμα

verses.restored: He kept back from the price, his wife also knowing it, and bringing a certain part, laid it at the apostles' feet.

familiar.text: And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

modern.text: With his wife’s full knowledge, he kept back some of the proceeds for himself, but brought a portion and laid it at the apostles’ feet.

original.text: καὶ ἐνοσφίσατο ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς, συνειδυίης καὶ τῆς ⸀γυναικός, καὶ ἐνέγκας μέρος τι παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων ἔθηκεν.

verses.restored: Peter said, Ananias, why has the adversarial impulse filled your heart to lie to the holy Spirit and keep back from the price of the field?

familiar.text: But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?

modern.text: Then Peter said, “Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and withhold some of the proceeds from the land?

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ⸀ὁ Πέτρος· Ἁνανία, διὰ τί ἐπλήρωσεν ὁ Σατανᾶς τὴν καρδίαν σου, ψεύσασθαί σε τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καὶ ⸀νοσφίσασθαι ἀπὸ τῆς τιμῆς τοῦ χωρίου;

verses.restored: While remaining, did it not remain yours? And after being sold, was it not in your authority? Why did you set this deed in your heart? You did not lie to humans but to the Divine.

familiar.text: Whiles it remained, was it not thine own? and after it was sold, was it not in thine own power? why hast thou conceived this thing in thine heart? thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.

modern.text: Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How could you conceive such a deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God!”

original.text: οὐχὶ μένον σοὶ ἔμενεν καὶ πραθὲν ἐν τῇ σῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ὑπῆρχεν; τί ὅτι ἔθου ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ σου τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο; οὐκ ἐψεύσω ἀνθρώποις ἀλλὰ τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: Hearing these words, Ananias fell down and breathed out; great awe came upon all who heard.

familiar.text: And Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.

modern.text: On hearing these words, Ananias fell down and died. And great fear came over all who heard what had happened.

original.text: ἀκούων δὲ ὁ Ἁνανίας τοὺς λόγους τούτους πεσὼν ἐξέψυξεν· καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ⸀ἀκούοντας.

verses.restored: The younger ones rose, wrapped him, carried him out, and buried him.

familiar.text: And the young men arose, wound him up, and carried him out, and buried him.

modern.text: Then the young men stepped forward, wrapped up his body, and carried him out and buried him.

original.text: ἀναστάντες δὲ οἱ νεώτεροι συνέστειλαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν.

verses.restored: It happened about three hours later that his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.

familiar.text: And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in.

modern.text: About three hours later his wife also came in, unaware of what had happened.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ὡς ὡρῶν τριῶν διάστημα καὶ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ μὴ εἰδυῖα τὸ γεγονὸς εἰσῆλθεν.

verses.restored: Peter answered her, Tell me whether you sold the field for so much. She said, Yes, for so much.

familiar.text: And Peter answered unto her, Tell me whether ye sold the land for so much? And she said, Yea, for so much.

modern.text: “Tell me,” said Peter, “is this the price you and your husband got for the land?” “Yes,” she answered, “that is the price.”

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ⸂πρὸς αὐτὴν⸃ ⸀Πέτρος· Εἰπέ μοι, εἰ τοσούτου τὸ χωρίον ἀπέδοσθε; ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· Ναί, τοσούτου.

verses.restored: Peter said to her, Why was it agreed by you to test the Spirit of the Lord? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out.

familiar.text: Then Peter said unto her, How is it that ye have agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord? behold, the feet of them which have buried thy husband are at the door, and shall carry thee out.

modern.text: “How could you agree to test the Spirit of the Lord?” Peter replied. “Look, the feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out also.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ⸀Πέτρος πρὸς αὐτήν· Τί ὅτι συνεφωνήθη ὑμῖν πειράσαι τὸ πνεῦμα κυρίου; ἰδοὺ οἱ πόδες τῶν θαψάντων τὸν ἄνδρα σου ἐπὶ τῇ θύρᾳ καὶ ἐξοίσουσίν σε.

verses.restored: Immediately she fell at his feet and breathed out. The young ones came in and found her dead, and carrying her out, buried her beside her husband.

familiar.text: Then fell she down straightway at his feet, and yielded up the ghost: and the young men came in, and found her dead, and, carrying her forth, buried her by her husband.

modern.text: At that instant she fell down at his feet and died. Then the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband.

original.text: ἔπεσεν δὲ παραχρῆμα ⸀πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξέψυξεν· εἰσελθόντες δὲ οἱ νεανίσκοι εὗρον αὐτὴν νεκράν, καὶ ἐξενέγκαντες ἔθαψαν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα αὐτῆς.

verses.restored: Great awe came upon the whole assembly and upon all who heard these things.

familiar.text: And great fear came upon all the church, and upon as many as heard these things.

modern.text: And great fear came over the whole church and all who heard about these events. The Apostles Heal Many

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο φόβος μέγας ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἐπὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντας ταῦτα.

verses.restored: Through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were happening among the people, and they were all with one accord in Solomon's Portico.

familiar.text: And by the hands of the apostles were many signs and wonders wrought among the people; (and they were all with one accord in Solomon’s porch.

modern.text: The apostles performed many signs and wonders among the people, and with one accord the believers gathered together in Solomon’s Colonnade.

original.text: Διὰ δὲ τῶν χειρῶν τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ⸂πολλὰ ἐν τῷ λαῷ⸃· καὶ ἦσαν ὁμοθυμαδὸν ⸀ἅπαντες ἐν τῇ Στοᾷ Σολομῶντος·

verses.restored: None of the rest dared join themselves to them, yet the people magnified them.

familiar.text: And of the rest durst no man join himself to them: but the people magnified them.

modern.text: Although the people regarded them highly, no one else dared to join them.

original.text: τῶν δὲ λοιπῶν οὐδεὶς ἐτόλμα κολλᾶσθαι αὐτοῖς, ἀλλʼ ἐμεγάλυνεν αὐτοὺς ὁ λαός,

verses.restored: More than ever, those trusting in the Lord were added, multitudes of both men and women.

familiar.text: And believers were the more added to the Lord, multitudes both of men and women.)

modern.text: Yet more and more believers were brought to the Lord—large numbers of both men and women.

original.text: μᾶλλον δὲ προσετίθεντο πιστεύοντες τῷ κυρίῳ πλήθη ἀνδρῶν τε καὶ γυναικῶν·

verses.restored: So they even carried the weak into the streets and placed them on beds and mats, so that as Peter came, even his shadow might overshadow some of them.

familiar.text: Insomuch that they brought forth the sick into the streets, and laid them on beds and couches, that at the least the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them.

modern.text: As a result, people brought the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that at least Peter’s shadow might fall on some of them as he passed by.

original.text: ὥστε ⸂καὶ εἰς⸃ τὰς πλατείας ἐκφέρειν τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς καὶ τιθέναι ἐπὶ ⸀κλιναρίων καὶ κραβάττων, ἵνα ἐρχομένου Πέτρου κἂν ἡ σκιὰ ⸀ἐπισκιάσῃ τινὶ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: The multitude also from the cities around Jerusalem came together, carrying the weak and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all being healed.

familiar.text: There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.

modern.text: Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed. The Apostles Arrested and Freed

original.text: συνήρχετο δὲ καὶ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν πέριξ ⸀πόλεων Ἰερουσαλήμ, φέροντες ἀσθενεῖς καὶ ὀχλουμένους ὑπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων, οἵτινες ἐθεραπεύοντο ἅπαντες.

verses.restored: But the high priest rose up, and all those with him, the party of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy.

familiar.text: Then the high priest rose up, and all they that were with him, (which is the sect of the Sadducees,) and were filled with indignation,

modern.text: Then the high priest and all his associates, who belonged to the party of the Sadducees, were filled with jealousy. They went out

original.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ πάντες οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ, ἡ οὖσα αἵρεσις τῶν Σαδδουκαίων, ἐπλήσθησαν ζήλου

verses.restored: They laid hands on the apostles and put them in public custody.

familiar.text: And laid their hands on the apostles, and put them in the common prison.

modern.text: and arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.

original.text: καὶ ἐπέβαλον τὰς ⸀χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ ἔθεντο αὐτοὺς ἐν τηρήσει δημοσίᾳ.

verses.restored: But during the night a messenger of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, brought them out, and said,

familiar.text: But the angel of the Lord by night opened the prison doors, and brought them forth, and said,

modern.text: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying,

original.text: ἄγγελος δὲ κυρίου ⸀διὰ νυκτὸς ⸀ἤνοιξε τὰς θύρας τῆς φυλακῆς ἐξαγαγών τε αὐτοὺς εἶπεν·

verses.restored: Go, stand in the temple and speak to the people all the words of this life.

familiar.text: Go, stand and speak in the temple to the people all the words of this life.

modern.text: “Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people the full message of this new life.”

original.text: Πορεύεσθε καὶ σταθέντες λαλεῖτε ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τῷ λαῷ πάντα τὰ ῥήματα τῆς ζωῆς ταύτης.

verses.restored: Hearing this, they entered the temple at daybreak and were teaching. The high priest came, and those with him, and called together the council and all the elders of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

familiar.text: And when they heard that, they entered into the temple early in the morning, and taught. But the high priest came, and they that were with him, and called the council together, and all the senate of the children of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.

modern.text: At daybreak the apostles entered the temple courts as they had been told and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his associates arrived, they convened the Sanhedrin —the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail for the apostles.

original.text: ἀκούσαντες δὲ εἰσῆλθον ὑπὸ τὸν ὄρθρον εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἐδίδασκον. Παραγενόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ οἱ σὺν αὐτῷ συνεκάλεσαν τὸ συνέδριον καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γερουσίαν τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν εἰς τὸ δεσμωτήριον ἀχθῆναι αὐτούς.

verses.restored: But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison, and returning, reported,

familiar.text: But when the officers came, and found them not in the prison, they returned, and told,

modern.text: But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they returned with the report:

original.text: οἱ δὲ ⸂παραγενόμενοι ὑπηρέται⸃ οὐχ εὗρον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ, ἀναστρέψαντες δὲ ἀπήγγειλαν

verses.restored: saying, We found the prison locked with all security and the guards standing at the doors, but opening, we found no one inside.

familiar.text: Saying, The prison truly found we shut with all safety, and the keepers standing without before the doors: but when we had opened, we found no man within.

modern.text: “We found the jail securely locked, with the guards posted at the doors; but when we opened them, we found no one inside.” The Apostles before the Sanhedrin

original.text: λέγοντες ὅτι ⸀Τὸ δεσμωτήριον εὕρομεν κεκλεισμένον ἐν πάσῃ ἀσφαλείᾳ καὶ τοὺς φύλακας ἑστῶτας ⸀ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν, ἀνοίξαντες δὲ ἔσω οὐδένα εὕρομεν.

verses.restored: When the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were perplexed about them, what this might become.

familiar.text: Now when the high priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these things, they doubted of them whereunto this would grow.

modern.text: When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this account, they were perplexed as to what was happening.

original.text: ὡς δὲ ἤκουσαν τοὺς λόγους τούτους ὅ ⸀τε στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, διηπόρουν περὶ αὐτῶν τί ἂν γένοιτο τοῦτο.

verses.restored: Someone came and reported to them, Look, the men whom you put in prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people.

familiar.text: Then came one and told them, saying, Behold, the men whom ye put in prison are standing in the temple, and teaching the people.

modern.text: Then someone came in and announced, “Look, the men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people!”

original.text: παραγενόμενος δέ τις ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Ἰδοὺ οἱ ἄνδρες οὓς ἔθεσθε ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ εἰσὶν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἑστῶτες καὶ διδάσκοντες τὸν λαόν.

verses.restored: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them, not with force, for they feared the people, lest they be stoned.

familiar.text: Then went the captain with the officers, and brought them without violence: for they feared the people, lest they should have been stoned.

modern.text: At that point, the captain went with the officers and brought the apostles—but not by force, for fear the people would stone them.

original.text: τότε ἀπελθὼν ὁ στρατηγὸς σὺν τοῖς ὑπηρέταις ⸀ἤγαγεν αὐτούς, οὐ μετὰ βίας, ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ τὸν λαόν, ⸀μὴ λιθασθῶσιν.

verses.restored: Bringing them, they stood them in the council, and the high priest questioned them,

familiar.text: And when they had brought them, they set them before the council: and the high priest asked them,

modern.text: They brought them in and made them stand before the Sanhedrin, where the high priest interrogated them.

original.text: Ἀγαγόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔστησαν ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ. καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτοὺς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς

verses.restored: saying, We strictly commanded you not to teach in this name, and look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and intend to bring this human's blood upon us.

familiar.text: Saying, Did not we straitly command you that ye should not teach in this name? and, behold, ye have filled Jerusalem with your doctrine, and intend to bring this man’s blood upon us.

modern.text: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name,” he said. “Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching and are determined to make us responsible for this man’s blood.”

original.text: ⸀λέγων· Παραγγελίᾳ παρηγγείλαμεν ὑμῖν μὴ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ, καὶ ἰδοὺ πεπληρώκατε τὴν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τῆς διδαχῆς ὑμῶν, καὶ βούλεσθε ἐπαγαγεῖν ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου.

verses.restored: Peter and the apostles answered, It is necessary to obey the Divine rather than humans.

familiar.text: Then Peter and the other apostles answered and said, We ought to obey God rather than men.

modern.text: But Peter and the other apostles replied, “We must obey God rather than men.

original.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Πέτρος καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι εἶπαν· Πειθαρχεῖν δεῖ θεῷ μᾶλλον ἢ ἀνθρώποις.

verses.restored: The Divine of our fathers raised Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.

familiar.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.

modern.text: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you had killed by hanging Him on a tree.

original.text: ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων ἡμῶν ἤγειρεν Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς διεχειρίσασθε κρεμάσαντες ἐπὶ ξύλου·

verses.restored: This one the Divine exalted at his right hand as Leader and Savior/Healer, to give turning/realignment to Israel and release of sins/misalignments.

familiar.text: Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.

modern.text: God exalted Him to His right hand as Prince and Savior, in order to grant repentance and forgiveness of sins to Israel.

original.text: τοῦτον ὁ θεὸς ἀρχηγὸν καὶ σωτῆρα ὕψωσεν τῇ δεξιᾷ αὐτοῦ, ⸀τοῦ δοῦναι μετάνοιαν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν·

verses.restored: We are witnesses of these words, and so is the holy Spirit whom the Divine gave to those obeying him.

familiar.text: And we are his witnesses of these things; and so is also the Holy Ghost, whom God hath given to them that obey him.

modern.text: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.” Gamaliel’s Advice

original.text: καὶ ἡμεῖς ⸀ἐσμεν μάρτυρες τῶν ῥημάτων τούτων, καὶ τὸ ⸀πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς τοῖς πειθαρχοῦσιν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Hearing this, they were cut through and were intending to kill them.

familiar.text: When they heard that, they were cut to the heart, and took counsel to slay them.

modern.text: When the Council members heard this, they were enraged, and they resolved to put the apostles to death.

original.text: Οἱ δὲ ⸀ἀκούσαντες διεπρίοντο καὶ ἐβούλοντο ἀνελεῖν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: But a certain Pharisee in the council, Gamaliel by name, a teacher of the Law honored by all the people, rose and commanded that the humans be put outside for a little while.

familiar.text: Then stood there up one in the council, a Pharisee, named Gamaliel, a doctor of the law, had in reputation among all the people, and commanded to put the apostles forth a little space;

modern.text: But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the Sanhedrin and ordered that the men be put outside for a short time.

original.text: ἀναστὰς δέ τις ἐν τῷ συνεδρίῳ Φαρισαῖος ὀνόματι Γαμαλιήλ, νομοδιδάσκαλος τίμιος παντὶ τῷ λαῷ, ἐκέλευσεν ἔξω ⸀βραχὺ τοὺς ⸀ἀνθρώπους ποιῆσαι,

verses.restored: He said to them, Men of Israel, take care for yourselves concerning these humans, what you are about to do.

familiar.text: And said unto them, Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.

modern.text: “Men of Israel,” he said, “consider carefully what you are about to do to these men.

original.text: εἶπέν τε πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις τί μέλλετε πράσσειν.

verses.restored: For before these days Theudas rose, saying he himself was someone, to whom a number of men, about four hundred, attached themselves; he was killed, and all who were persuaded by him were dissolved and came to nothing.

familiar.text: For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.

modern.text: Some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, all his followers were dispersed, and it all came to nothing.

original.text: πρὸ γὰρ τούτων τῶν ἡμερῶν ἀνέστη Θευδᾶς, λέγων εἶναί τινα ἑαυτόν, ᾧ ⸀προσεκλίθη ⸂ἀνδρῶν ἀριθμὸς ὡς⸃ τετρακοσίων· ὃς ἀνῃρέθη, καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διελύθησαν καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς οὐδέν.

verses.restored: After this Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the registration and drew away people after him; that one also perished, and all who were persuaded by him were scattered.

familiar.text: After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.

modern.text: After him, Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew away people after him. He too perished, and all his followers were scattered.

original.text: μετὰ τοῦτον ἀνέστη Ἰούδας ὁ Γαλιλαῖος ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς ἀπογραφῆς καὶ ἀπέστησε ⸀λαὸν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ· κἀκεῖνος ἀπώλετο καὶ πάντες ὅσοι ἐπείθοντο αὐτῷ διεσκορπίσθησαν.

verses.restored: And now I say to you, stand away from these humans and release them; because if this counsel or work is from humans, it will be overthrown.

familiar.text: And now I say unto you, Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought:

modern.text: So in the present case I advise you: Leave these men alone. Let them go! For if their purpose or endeavor is of human origin, it will fail.

original.text: καὶ τὰ νῦν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπόστητε ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων τούτων καὶ ⸀ἄφετε αὐτούς· (ὅτι ἐὰν ᾖ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἡ βουλὴ ⸀αὕτη ἢ τὸ ἔργον τοῦτο, καταλυθήσεται,

verses.restored: But if it is from the Divine, you will not be able to overthrow them, lest you even be found fighting against the Divine.

familiar.text: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.

modern.text: But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God.”

original.text: εἰ δὲ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐστιν, οὐ ⸀δυνήσεσθε καταλῦσαι ⸀αὐτούς·) μήποτε καὶ θεομάχοι εὑρεθῆτε. ἐπείσθησαν δὲ αὐτῷ,

verses.restored: They were persuaded by him, and calling the apostles, they beat them, commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.

familiar.text: And to him they agreed: and when they had called the apostles, and beaten them, they commanded that they should not speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.

modern.text: At this, they yielded to Gamaliel. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and released them.

original.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενοι τοὺς ἀποστόλους δείραντες παρήγγειλαν μὴ λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ καὶ ⸀ἀπέλυσαν.

verses.restored: Therefore they went from the face of the council rejoicing that they were considered worthy to be dishonored for the Name.

familiar.text: And they departed from the presence of the council, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.

modern.text: The apostles left the Sanhedrin, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy of suffering disgrace for the Name.

original.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἐπορεύοντο χαίροντες ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ συνεδρίου ὅτι ⸂κατηξιώθησαν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος⸃ ἀτιμασθῆναι·

verses.restored: Every day, in the temple and house by house, they did not cease teaching and announcing the good news: Jesus the Messiah.

familiar.text: And daily in the temple, and in every house, they ceased not to teach and preach Jesus Christ.

modern.text: Every day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they did not stop teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.

original.text: πᾶσάν τε ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ κατʼ οἶκον οὐκ ἐπαύοντο διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι ⸂τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν⸃.
